subject.role: qsa_prefill:layers.{3,7,...,47}.attn_q - the prefill attention path for the full-attention (non-QSA) layers

host.gpu: AMD Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo APU), per benchmarks/README.md

measurement.note: raw CSV holds two prefill passes; all figures are 1x

launch_split.source: measured durations, grouped by grid; context assignment inferred and cross-checked
launch_split.cross_check: The three launches agree at 23.2 / 25.9 / 37.5 ns per (row, context-token) pair, a 1.6x spread across a 3-row launch and two 1024-row launches. That uniformity is what supports the context assignment; the context lengths are not directly observable in the trace because context_len arrives as a device pointer.
launch_split.grid_semantics: rocprofv3 Grid_Size_X/Y are total work-items: 6144/256 = 24 = query heads, 1024/1 = 1024 = query rows.

correction.cause: raw 2-pass CSV read as 1x, and the layer count taken as 48/2 instead of 48/4
correction.authority: role-analysis.json exact_role_kernels: 12 entries qsa_prefill:layers.{3,7,11,15,19,23,27,31,35,39,43,47}.attn_q, rows=3 each, 66.70-66.84 ms each
correction.note: full_attention_interval=4 gives 48/4 = 12 layers, matching compress_ratios having a nonzero every fourth position

roofline.verdict: Not compute-bound (3.2% of FP32 peak) and not DRAM-bound. It demands ~968 GB/s of L1-level K/V load traffic against 100.7 MB of unique data, a 7707x re-read, because every (head, row) block rescans the whole context.

structure.decomposition: one block per (query head, query row): grid (24, 1024), 256 threads, 8 warps
structure.qk_phase: warp-per-token loop. Per token: 256 dims / 32 lanes = 8 FMA per lane, then a 5-step shuffle + 5 adds to reduce to ONE score, written to LDS by lane 0 only. 18 lane-instructions per 8 useful FMAs - 125% reduction overhead.
structure.pv_phase: value_groups == 1 because threads=256 < 512. Each of the 256 threads holds VALUE_VECTOR=2 output dims and serially scans ALL context_len tokens: one LDS read of scores[token], one coalesced global bf16 read, two FMA.
structure.three_passes_over_context: 1) QK + running max, 2) exp + sum, 3) PV. The scores vector for the whole context lives in LDS between them.
structure.no_cross_row_reuse: row = blockIdx.y, so every query row rescans the context independently. No row tiling and no GQA blocking: the 12 query heads sharing a kv_head are separate blocks with no shared K/V read.

occupancy.note: the trailing max_context_len*8 is the int64 token_offsets table, present only in the <true, N> leaves
occupancy.verdict: LDS-limited, and the limit tightens with context length - the 54.30 ms launch (81% of the kernel) runs at 25% occupancy. The int64 token_offsets table is 16 KB of the 26 KB, i.e. 61% of the LDS at context 2048, and it is the single largest consumer.
occupancy.max_offset_fits_int32: physical_block*block_size + block_offset, times num_kv_heads*head_dim = 2*256 = 512. At a 4096-token context the largest offset is 4096*512 = 2.1e6; int32 holds any context up to ~4M tokens.

levers.lever: narrow token_offsets from int64 to int32
levers.why: changes only an address table's width. The accumulation order, the shuffle tree, the wave reduction, and the softmax are untouched.
levers.effect: at context 2048: 26.04 -> 18.04 KB/block, 2 -> 3 blocks/CU, 25% -> 38% occupancy. At context 1024: 14.04 -> 10.04 KB, 4 -> 6 blocks/CU, 50% -> 75%.
levers.cost: a template parameter or a second entry point; the <true, N> leaf's shared_bytes formula changes
levers.risk: low. The <false, N> leaves must keep their existing allocation, since they do not declare the table.
levers.estimated_prize_basis: occupancy is the most likely limiter and this is the only occupancy lever with no arithmetic risk, but the occupancy-to-time mapping is not measured here

levers.lever: stop storing the whole scores vector in LDS (tile the context, flash-style)
levers.why: the scores array is max_context_len floats (8 KB at 2048) and forces three separate passes over the context with two __syncthreads each. Tiling the context so scores stay in registers removes the array entirely and collapses the three passes into one, which is the standard fix for exactly this shape.
levers.cost: a real rewrite of the leaf; the online-softmax rescaling changes the accumulation order
levers.risk: high - needs the production numerical gate and a registered strict fallback
levers.estimated_prize_basis: this is the lever that removes the occupancy ceiling rather than moving it; magnitude unmeasured

levers.lever: GQA blocking: process the 12 query heads of a kv_head in one block
levers.arithmetic: preserving if each head keeps its own 8-warp reduction set
levers.why: cuts K/V load traffic by up to 12x, from 776 GB to 64.7 GB. The heads are independent, so a per-head reduction that keeps its own warp set and token striding is bit-exact.
levers.cost: LDS scales with the head group: scores for 12 heads x 2048 context is 96 KB, which does not fit. A group of 2-4 heads is 16-32 KB on top of the current 26 KB, so this competes with lever 1 for the same LDS budget and probably needs lever 2 first.
levers.risk: medium - feasible only in combination with a smaller scores footprint

levers.lever: row tiling: multiple query rows per block
levers.arithmetic: changing unless each row keeps its own warp set
levers.why: reuses the K/V scan and the token-offset table across rows. Bit-exact only if each row keeps 8 warps and the same token striding, which multiplies LDS by the row count.
levers.cost: same LDS budget conflict as lever 3

levers.lever: fold inv_denom into the PV accumulation to drop the normalisation pass
levers.why: the value_groups==1 path runs a full pass over context_len where only lane 0 of each warp is active, doing scores[token] *= inv_denom. The value_groups>1 path already folds it as (scores[token] * inv_denom), which produces identical values in an identical order.
levers.effect: removes context_len/num_warps iterations of a 31/32-idle pass per block, plus one __syncthreads
levers.cost: small edit to the value_groups==1 path
levers.risk: low, but it is 0.5% of the kernel at most

not_established: The precise hardware limiter is not isolated. Three candidates are each consistent with the measurements - LDS-limited occupancy at 25%, the 968 GB/s redundant K/V load stream, and the 125% shuffle-reduction overhead per score - and no counter in the trace separates them. Ranking the levers above rests on structural argument, not on a measured counter attribution.
The context lengths per launch are inferred from the ns-per-pair cross-check, not read from context_len_ptr, which is a device pointer.
The 54.30 ms launch has not been isolated in a standalone microbenchmark, so no per-lever prize is estimated.
